finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar makes a server-side GET to an attacker-chosen URL. The only check is an https:// prefix, which constrains neither host nor redirect target, so the request can reach internal hosts or cloud metadata.

trace.note: Unauthenticated POST route; no auth middleware on the app.
Guard: typeof url === 'string' && url.startsWith('https://'). Rejects non-https, but any https host passes, including https://127.0.0.1, https://10.x, https://users.internal:8080.

axios.get(url) with no host allow-list, no IP/private-range check, no DNS pinning, no maxRedirects: 0, and no beforeRedirect re-validation. Axios follows redirects by default, so a public https:// URL that 302s to http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/ is fetched without any check.
Response size (img.data.length) is returned to the caller, giving an oracle on response size even though the body is not returned.

finding.guards_checked: Type check (string only; not an SSRF control). Scheme check via raw startsWith('https://'); restricts scheme only, not host, port, IP range, or redirects. No host allow-list, IP-range denylist, or post-DNS check exists in server.js. No redirect control; axios defaults apply (redirects followed). axios is not pinned in the repo (no package.json), so this relies on axios default behaviour. Only a byte length is returned, which limits direct exfiltration but still allows internal probing and triggering of side-effecting GET requests.

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:11 is a type check plus a scheme-only startsWith("https://") check, which does not constrain host, IP range, port, or redirects. server.js:14 has no host allow-list, IP check, or maxRedirects/beforeRedirect control. No auth middleware is registered on the app (server.js:5 is only express.json()).
verdict.reason: The POST /profile/avatar route at server.js:9 has no auth, req.body.avatarUrl at server.js:10 is attacker-supplied, and the only check at server.js:11 is a scheme prefix, so axios.get at server.js:14 will reach any https host, including one that redirects to internal targets, and server.js:15 returns the response size as an oracle.
